item.title: Indiana Approves Student-Centered K-12 Accountability Model
item.description: After eight months of stakeholder feedback, the Indiana State Board of Education approved the final K-12 accountability rule on Wednesday, March 4.

item.title: Governors Orders Flags Half-staff In Lou Holtz’s Honor March 9
item.description: Flags across Indiana are set to be flown at half-staff Monday, March 9 in honor of former Notre Dame Fighting Irish football coach Lou Holtz.

item.title: Claypool Man Arrested After Failing To Update Information On Sex Offender Registry
item.description: A Claypool man has been arrested for allegedly not registering as a sex offender after being evicted from a property.

item.title: Indiana Supreme Court Upholds COVID-19 Immunity In Patient Death Case
item.description: Hospitals and other medical providers cannot be held liable for complications that developed while treating a patient for COVID-19 during the pandemic emergency, the Indiana Supreme Court ruled Wednesday, March 4.

item.title: Tait Comes Home To Welcoming Audience
item.description: Syracuse native Lauren Tait came home to a warm welcome as she was the featured speaker at this year’s LeadHERship luncheon, hosted by the Syracuse-Wawasee Chamber of Commerce Thursday, March 5.

item.title: Warsaw Parks Department Hosting Free Arts & Crafts Day
item.description: The City of Warsaw Parks and Recreation Department invites the community to a free arts and crafts day at Pete Thorn Gym from 1-3 p.m. Wednesday, March 11.

item.title: INDOT Presents Proposed SR 33 Widening Project
item.description: The Indiana Department of Transportation held a public meeting Wednesday, March 3 in Goshen to present plans for a proposed widening and reconstruction project along SR 33 aimed at improving safety and traffic flow.

item.title: Severe Thunderstorm Watch Issued For Kosciusko County, Surrounding Areas
item.description: The National Weather Service of Northern Indiana has issued a Severe Thunderstorm Watch for Kosciusko County and surrounding areas until 11 p.m. Friday, March 6.
